patch_description:
This replaces selected two-hop rewards with an all-hop routing proxy. A demand-biased fractional network defines a discounted walk resolvent, which measures connectivity through paths of every length.

Exact binary finite differences of this proxy produce link rewards and interactions: complementary links receive rewards, while competing alternatives can receive penalties. Unlike a Taylor expansion, these differences remain well behaved when a link changes from a small fractional value to one. Degree-invariant components are removed, and sparse interactions are retained with a mean-field correction for discarded terms.

The construction is deterministic, uses no routing solver, and generates fewer than \(2n^3\) candidate couplings before sparsification. Its intended advantage is size-consistent, saturation-aware ranking rather than adding more independently rewarded paths; improvement still requires evaluation.
